codeReview.summary: The unified scope model and most scoped/filter/reset behaviors line up with the feature contract, but refresh does not reliably preserve the active narrowed state because search input is debounced while refresh reads stale filter state immediately.

issues.description: The search field only syncs `appState.view.filters.search` inside a 200ms debounce (`els.search.addEventListener('input', ...)`), while the refresh button immediately calls `fetchSheetData()` (`app.js:900`). If the user types a search term and clicks Refresh before the debounce fires, `fetchSheetData()` re-renders using the old empty search filter, so the narrowed state is not preserved after refresh. That violates VAL-CROSS-003's requirement that refresh preserve coherent scoped/filtered state. The new refresh test also misses this because it uses `page.fill()` and waits for the filtered count before clicking refresh (`tests/dashboard-state-seams.spec.js:169-187`), so it never exercises the race.

summary: I reviewed the mission feature metadata, the worker transcript skeleton, the handoff, the `static-dashboard-worker` skill, mission shared-state artifacts, and commit `baa7e30f59f32c40f0a5661f025acb64eac342b8`. The scope refactor largely satisfies the blocked/search/filter/reset requirements, but there is one blocking correctness gap: refresh can drop a just-entered search term because the search state is debounced and not flushed before `fetchSheetData()` runs, so the implementation does not fully satisfy the required coherent refresh behavior under active narrowing.
